keyFindings.text: Keep the current first-glance hierarchy and spacious framing: the 64 px title, 28 px subtitle, 24 px section labels, 20 px nodes, 16 px supporting text, white board section, generous margins, aligned key, and source line create a legible entry order; user-flow, ER, and gantt examples show distinct layouts while retaining the same title and key grammar. [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-create-figjam/assets/compose-board.js:87-103,1125-1140,1142-1150,1194-1202; AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-create-figjam/references/style-guide.md:189-204; AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-create-figjam/assets/screenshots/README.md:25-33; visual: user-flow-board.png, er-board.png, gantt-board.png]

Preserve meaning-based color, shape, and key semantics across types: kind-to-shape/color mappings are shared, the pink accent is reserved for the chosen first-glance object, and the key explains marks; sequence arrows, state roles, and architecture lanes deliberately retain different type-specific semantics within that common grammar. [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-create-figjam/references/style-guide.md:28-36,40-82,83-95,137-152; AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-create-figjam/references/types/sequence.md:47-58; AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-create-figjam/references/types/state.md:48-54; AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-create-figjam/references/types/architecture.md:42-53]

Prioritize compact back-edge routing and sequence overview legibility: state-board.png and state-on-existing-board.png show return transitions making long perimeter loops, process-board.png shows long lane trunks, and sequence-board.png is the lowest-scoring type at 19/22 while keeping a much taller lifeline layout; the gallery scores the other seven boards 21–22/22. Tune route length, label placement, and type-specific density without weakening read-back fidelity. [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-create-figjam/assets/screenshots/README.md:25-33; AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-create-figjam/assets/compose-board.js:600-623; AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-create-figjam/references/types/sequence.md:47-58; visual: state-board.png, state-on-existing-board.png, process-board.png, sequence-board.png]

The design record is split across a style guide, JavaScript constants, Python checks, and a hand-copied Project composer: the guide claims to be the one source for color/type/spacing, but SHAPE, TINT, KINDS, TYPE, GRID and gaps live in compose-board.js, accepted pairs live in common.py, and the Project mirror parity check compares the compact JavaScript block only. This creates a clear need for a validated shared specification while preserving the current swatch and contrast rules. Unify the design score contract before changing visuals: quality-rubric.md Section 7 scores eight criteria out of 16, while the playbook and screenshot README use a 22-point total with extra crossings, shared-trunk, label-collision, hygiene, and reply checks; the current gallery therefore cannot be compared from the rubric alone. Name one canonical 22-point scorecard or explicitly label the 16-point design subtotal and its six operational points. Add explicit spec-conformance grading without conflating the two existing score scopes: have quality-rubric.md include a named token-fidelity check for the overview design and the playbook scorecard check color, type, spacing, shape/stroke, connector/arrowhead, zone/key/title/source, and accent against the effective spec at reading zoom. Keep the 16-point overview-design result distinct from the 22-point whole-board score; if both receive a 0–2 fidelity criterion, label the revised totals (18 and 24) and re-score the gallery. Correction to Iteration 1: the score totals describe different scopes rather than contradictory math. quality-rubric.md Section 7 scores eight overview-design criteria out of 16; the playbook’s 22-point whole-board score uses four overview measures, four reading-zoom measures, four invariants, and the reply. Keep both views but state their relationship explicitly; the gallery has nine entries, so eight screenshots besides sequence-board.png score 21–22/22. Define shared and type-specific tokens without changing what colors mean. The shared schema should cover paired fills/strokes/text by semantic kind; font family, weight and scale for title, subtitle, zone/key, node, edge, field and source; grid and spacing; shape stroke and supported rounding; connector line, dash, weight and arrow caps; zone tints; key/title/source surfaces; and the first-glance accent. Add per-type token groups for sequence request/reply/async arrows and pins, state start/final/choice, architecture lanes, ER relationships, gantt status/milestone, and flow/process lanes or branches, while keeping role names and one accent invariant. Expose spacing as a constrained scale and make radius support honest: keep grid values on the configured base grid, bound minimum label sizes and route clearances, and reject negative or unusable dimensions. The current shape function sets FigJam shapeType and resizes the object but has no radius assignment, so document rounded-rectangle geometry as fixed until the composer adds and checks an API-supported radius control. [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-create-figjam/assets/compose-board.js:87-98,172-184,214-239; AI Systems/Product Owner/Product Owner/sk-create-figjam/references/style-guide.md:189-204]

Keep the one-call FigJam path deterministic: compose_board.py should extract only the designated JSON block, validate it, serialize the validated token object alongside MODEL, and fill the JavaScript composer’s STYLE placeholder before the existing size check. The composer can then use STYLE for paint, typography, geometry, connectors, zones, title, key, and source in its current single call; it should not expect the Figma runtime to read DESIGN.md from disk. [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-create-figjam/scripts/compose_board.py:69-77,578-606; AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-create-figjam/assets/compose-board.js:148-240,1125-1202]

Make the token schema the one palette authority for templates, examples, and checks as well as drawing. Shipped Mermaid templates and examples currently contain literal FigJam hex pairs for focus steps and neutral lanes; update flow_check.py and common.py to validate semantic roles against the active design block, and let compose_board.py draw the role from the spec rather than treating an example hex as the style source. [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-create-figjam/assets/templates/process.md:38-48,50-78; AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-create-figjam/assets/examples/process-fernhouse-refund.md:87-94; AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-create-figjam/references/style-guide.md:18-22,99-105,212-215]

Put the editable reference at packet scope: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-create-figjam/DESIGN.md is specific to the composer that draws these boards and gives the repository user one visible place to restyle all seven types. Do not place the override at repository root or duplicate an editable copy there. Treat it as a forward-authored FigJam design contract, not as an output from sk-design-md-generator, whose Style Reference workflow measures existing web CSS and explicitly excludes brief-only authoring. [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-create-figjam/references/style-guide.md:18-22,26-28; .skilled/skills/sk-design/sk-design-md-generator/SKILL.md:12-14,42-46]

Treat the Project package as a hand-maintained mirror, not a filesystem reader. Put the same compact token block and STYLE use instructions in Product Owner - Assets - Flow Board Composer.md, then extend compose_board.py --self-test to compare both the compact code and token block; Product Owner/SYNC.md requires hand-written parity because the Project has no Python and the compiler is retired. [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-create-figjam/scripts/compose_board.py:71-76,925-929; AI Systems/Product Owner/SYNC.md:8-15; AI Systems/Product Owner/claude project/knowledge/Product Owner - Assets - Flow Board Composer.md:1-16]

Use a human-readable Style Reference with one strict, versioned JSON token block as its machine contract. Public DESIGN.md examples present a portable agent-facing guide and can identify a canonical source; the Design Tokens Community Group format supplies a useful typed JSON pattern with grouped values and descriptions, while its report is not a W3C Standard. Borrow that structure as a bounded subset rather than parsing arbitrary prose or claiming the packet file is an extracted site reference. [SOURCE: https://github.com/stella/stella/blob/main/DESIGN.md:190-194; https://github.com/dimabraven/design-md:203-232; https://www.w3.org/community/reports/design-tokens/CG-FINAL-format-20251028/:27-35,298-312,402-424]

Use strict all-or-nothing validation: if DESIGN.md is absent, compile the existing built-in values; if its JSON block is malformed, unsupported, incomplete, or outside safe ranges, stop before producing a board call and report the field errors. Enforce text contrast at 4.5:1, keep the 3.0:1 mark floor for marks that rely on stroke contrast, and preserve only the guide’s named low-contrast FigJam swatch/container exceptions where shape, labels, and key prevent color-only meaning.
